issues.evidence: The academic text says only "handed me over time and again"; no object such as suffering is stated.
issues.fix: You have handed me over again and again. I have suffered for a long time.

issues.evidence: Academic: "an instrument for action" (ལས་ཀྱི་སྤྱད); "for doing good" is not stated.
issues.fix: I will keep it like a tool for getting things done.

issues.span: Even a meditation master has a different level of thinking mind.
issues.evidence: Academic: yogis differ from one another in intellect, and are refuted by those successively higher; the children's line reads as if one master differs from something unnamed.
issues.fix: Meditation masters are not all equal in their thinking minds. A higher master proves a lower one wrong.

issues.evidence: Academic: "even a Buddha would cycle [in saṃsāra]"; the locked term for འཁོར་བ is "cycle of rebirth", while "world" is locked for འཇིག་རྟེན.
issues.fix: Since even a Buddha would keep going around in the cycle of rebirth, what is the use of the way of acting for awakening?

issues.span: Because of a special circumstance, a person can see that the mind shines to itself.
issues.evidence: Academic: the opponent argues that because the mind, endowed with other conditions, sees (objects), it is luminous to itself. The children's text says a person sees the mind shining, and turns "other conditions" into a "special circumstance".
issues.fix: Someone might say, "The mind has other circumstances to help it see, so it shines to itself."

issues.evidence: Academic: "the vase is seen"; nothing says the vase was hidden.
